runtimes.notes: Desktop NetPlay supports local-multiplayer GameCube/Wii titles. Matching Dolphin versions and matching game region/revision are important; identical dumps are strongly recommended. Wii NetPlay is documented as more temperamental than GameCube NetPlay.

xemu supports NAT, UDP Tunnel, and Bridged Adapter networking. UDP Tunnel is intended for xemu-to-xemu Internet play; Bridged Adapter is useful with real Xbox hardware and XLink Kai. Virtual Xbox MAC addresses must be unique.

Preferred PS1 runtime. Start with one authoritative DuckStation host plus Parsec because it minimizes setup. If measured or observed streaming latency is the limiting layer, Sunshine + Moonlight is an alternate remote-couch transport. If remote-couch remains unacceptable, evaluate Mednafen native netplay as a separate two-emulator topology.

Advanced PS1 latency fallback, not the default. Both players run matching local emulation/content and connect through a Mednafen netplay server. Mednafen uses save states for synchronization; important memory-card state should be backed up or isolated before netplay testing.
Nostalgia v0.1 does not assume a universal PCSX2 netplay layer. For local multiplayer titles, remote couch is the default starter path unless a game-specific network recipe is validated.

RetroArch netplay requires matching RetroArch/core/content and a deterministic, sufficiently performant core. Current Libretro FAQ explicitly says the netplay model is unsuitable for PSX/N64/Dreamcast/GameCube/Wii/3DS-class systems; do not use RetroArch netplay as a PS1 fallback.
Flycast Dojo focuses on netplay/replay and documents P2P Match Codes, direct-IP play, and virtual-LAN options. Matching game files are required for netplay.

transports.notes: Default remote-couch transport. One player hosts the emulator. Remote gamepads are exposed to the host as virtual controllers. Ensure each player maps to a distinct emulator controller slot. Guest controllers are created when guests press buttons; controller order can require host-side repair after reconnects.

Alternate remote-couch transport when Parsec's streaming path is suspected to be the latency bottleneck. Sunshine is the host and Moonlight is the client. On Windows, full virtual gamepad support requires the virtual-input setup documented by Sunshine.
Used with games whose original console LAN/System-Link mode is verified by XLink Kai. With xemu, use the bridged-network path described by xemu/XLink documentation.

packs.use_for: GameCube/Wii local multiplayer transported through Dolphin NetPlay
Original Xbox System Link over Internet or mixed emulator/real-hardware sessions
Local multiplayer games where one authoritative emulator host is simplest

PS1 campaign: begin with DuckStation + Parsec, test alternate streaming only when latency evidence warrants it, and escalate to Mednafen native netplay when local rendering on both players is worth the added setup
